name: Turbo Dash
description: A colorful endless runner platformer across ten named difficulty levels. Jump tripwires, ride springs, read portals, dodge crumbling and fake platforms, evolve mid-run, spend coins at a merchant balloon, keep a pet, and chase a live shared leaderboard.
author: CaisoGames AI Team

touch.description: Tap anywhere to jump, hold for a higher jump. Pause button in the top-right. Landscape recommended.

features: Three-stage in-run evolution: RUNNER -> WINGED (double jump) -> BLAZE (triple jump + glide)
Evolution Cores earned by completing missions, collected on the track ahead
Air jumps set velocity rather than adding it, so every one is a reliable recovery
Each successive air jump is weaker, keeping the height ceiling bounded
Gap sizes scale with each form's MEASURED reach, so evolving never trivialises the level
Stage score multipliers (x1.0 / x1.25 / x1.6) reward evolving early
Form resets on death - losing a BLAZE run is the strongest restart pressure in the game
Coyote time and jump buffering so deaths always feel earned
Coin combo multiplier up to x8, plus close-call and big-air bonuses
Three rotating missions per run with per-mission difficulty tiers
Persistent records, rank and lifetime coins via localStorage
Power-ups: magnet, shield, and a temporary extra air jump
Four crossfading biomes: Meadow, Sunset Ridge, Midnight, Frost Peaks
Screen shake, hit-stop, speed lines and WebAudio sound with no asset files
Full touch support with multi-finger hold tracking and iOS audio unlock
Boot screen that explains itself if a sandboxed viewer blocks its scripts
Shop with three slots: hats, back packs and trails, bought with coins earned by playing
Strong items are gated on a distance RECORD as well as price - price alone gates time, not skill
Item effects chosen so none can inflate a score: the coin bonus pays the wallet only, and the slow pack trades scoring rate for reaction time
Cloud leaderboard over the artifact db capability: live top 20, one row per player
Name prompt via a real HTML input, so phones get their keyboard and accessibility
The game is complete without the cloud - the board falls back to this device's best
Three lives (max five), so one fall no longer ends the run
Reviving COSTS an evolution stage and the coin combo, which is what keeps scores comparable
Rare heart pickups that appear more often the closer you are to losing
Final-life tension: a pulsing red vignette kept to the screen edges so hazards stay readable
Super Suit: hold to fly on a per-run flight budget that only drains while held, then burns down to a Turbo Pack
Ten named difficulty levels, each announcing the hazard it introduces
Crumbling platforms (level 3+) that shake, crack and collapse 0.8s after you land
Fake platforms (level 5+) placed as DECOYS in wide gaps, never on the route itself
Fakes carry a visible tell (translucent and drifting) so reading them is a skill, not a memory test
Merchant balloon: mid-run spending as a single jump-and-touch, with no menu and no pause
Pets: Coin Pup (wallet-only coin gathering), Scout Bird (marks fakes), Spark Cub (spares one revive penalty)
A single banner queue, so zone, level and evolution announcements never overwrite each other
Fourth evolution HERO: 4 jumps plus a rechargeable flight burst, earned by completing all three missions in one run
HERO's flight refills only while running on the ground, so hovering forever is impossible by construction
The wallet total and a savings goal are shown during play, on the game-over screen and in the shop
Coins are banked the moment they are collected, so abandoning a run mid-way (app switch, closed tab) loses nothing
A storage self-test at boot; if saving is blocked the title screen says so instead of failing silently
Losing a life freezes the run on a LIFE LOST screen until a tap, with CONTINUE and SHOP offered there
Every change is written to storage at once - no throttle, no unsaved window
Two on-disk copies: the previous state is rotated to a backup before each write, and a corrupt primary is recovered from it and repaired on the spot
Writes fire on pagehide, beforeunload, blur, freeze and visibilitychange, plus a 1s heartbeat while playing
A tick lights beside the wallet on every successful save, so saving is something the player can watch happen
Tripwires (level 2+): the first hazard, and the only one that never kills - run into one and you stumble for 0.37s with no jump
A wire is only placed where the platform runs on for the whole stun distance at top speed, so a stumble can never end at a pit
Springs (level 4+): a high, slow arc under halved gravity - long enough to see the landing and steer with an air jump
Portals (level 7+): both rings drawn so the exit is readable first; a warp pays +150 but skips the loot between and spends your air jumps
Skipped portal distance is never credited to distance, level, biome or speed
A 0.45s input lockout when the run stops, so the taps already in flight at the moment of death cannot dismiss the screen
LIFE LOST accepts only its CONTINUE button - never a stray tap - and shows WAIT while locked
A pause button in the top-right corner, with a PAUSED screen offering RESUME, SHOP, LEADERBOARD and END RUN
Escape toggles pause; a menu opened from the pause returns to the pause rather than into a running game

primary: Multi-jump physics with coyote time and jump buffering
unique: Missions pay out a visible ability rather than an abstract score bonus
A power curve inside a single run: weak, strong, unstoppable
Form is lost on death, so loss aversion drives the restart
Gaps sized from each form's measured physics, not an estimate
Shop perks are designed so buying power cannot buy leaderboard position
A revive costs a form and the combo, so three lives inflate scores x1.78 rather than the naive x3
Flight is a total budget per run, making WHEN to spend it the decision rather than whether to hold
Fake platforms are opt-in bait beside the route, so a trap is never a coin flip
Mid-run shopping is a pickup rather than a menu, because a menu would stop the run
Pets may ease the run or fatten the wallet, but never inflate the score
Flight is reachable by skill (HERO) as well as by purchase, keeping the game's rule that strong powers are earned
HERO's short rechargeable burst and the Super Suit's large one-shot budget stay distinct, so buying the suit still buys something
The stumble is the only non-lethal hazard, so it is the first one taught
A spring's slowness is its fairness: the arc is long enough to react to
A portal shows its exit before you commit, and costs air jumps and loot, so it is a decision rather than a gift
The stop screens are guarded against in-flight input, because a runner is played by tapping constantly
LIFE LOST is a decision screen so it needs a deliberate button; game over is a restart screen so tap-to-restart survives the lockout

difficulty.principle: One new hazard per level, never two, so there is always a stretch to learn each.

knownLimitations: Must be opened in a real browser or from a web address. In-app file previews (the sheet with an x and a share button) sandbox the page and block its scripts via CSP, which fires no error and does not trigger <noscript>; the game detects this and shows an explanation instead of a blank canvas.
Leaderboard identity is a per-browser id with a self-declared name. There is no verified user identity available to the page, so it is a friendly board rather than an anti-cheat system.

W and SPACE reach the name field while the prompt is open, and jump again once it closes

typing a real name through the browser's own input pipeline, on touch and mouse
a player outside the visible rows still has a findable, pinned rank

pagehide, beforeunload, blur, freeze and the 1s heartbeat each write
tripwires stumble without costing a life, block jumping only for the stun, and always leave recovery runway
springs fire only on a descending landing, arc high and slow under the ceiling, and yield to an air jump

stages.name: WINGED
stages.earnedBy: Complete one mission during the run, then collect the Evolution Core

stages.name: BLAZE
stages.earnedBy: Complete a second mission, then collect the next Core

stages.name: HERO
stages.earnedBy: Complete a third mission in the same run, then collect the Core

progression.note: Evolution is per-run and resets on death. Reaching HERO means completing all three missions in a single run. Mission tiers persist, so cores get harder to earn over time.

shop.currency: Coins collected while running, banked into a wallet at the end of each run
shop.designRule: Nothing sold may inflate a score. Coin bonuses pay the wallet only; the slow pack reduces scoring rate as well as difficulty; the strongest two items additionally require a distance record, because a price tag gates patience rather than skill.

items.effect: start each run with a shield
world 8% slower - and scoring 8% slower with it
Gathers coins; they pay the wallet, never the score
Once a run, a revive costs no evolution stage
Hold to fly from the opening second; 12s per run, then a Turbo Pack

leaderboard.shape: One document per player keyed by a per-browser id; live top 20 via orderBy(score,desc).limit(20).onSnapshot
leaderboard.identity: Self-declared name in localStorage. No verified user identity is available to the page, so this is a friendly board, not anti-cheat.
leaderboard.degradation: Outside the artifact viewer there is no window.claude at all, so the board falls back to this device's own best and the game is otherwise unchanged.
leaderboard.constraint: The db capability cannot be combined with public sharing, so the cloud build is organization-internal. A separate public build ships without db.
leaderboard.untrustedInput: Rows are written by other viewers: names are stripped of control characters and capped, and numbers are coerced before display.

lives.reviveCost: One evolution stage and the entire coin combo
lives.measuredInflation: x1.78 average score vs a single life, against a naive expectation of x3
lives.hearts: Rare pickups. Spawn chance is 0 at full health and rises to ~9% per platform on the last life.

merchant.form: A balloon on the track, reached with a deliberate jump
merchant.rationale: A mid-run menu would stop the run and, on a phone, appear under a finger already held down to jump. A priced pickup keeps the decision without breaking stride.
merchant.goods: Shown on the balloon before you commit; hearts are only offered when lives are missing.

economy.note: Earlier fix made the running total visible. This one fixes the remaining loss: coins were only credited in finishRun() on the final death, so any run abandoned mid-way lost them. They now bank on pickup and the profile is flushed whenever the page is hidden or unloaded.
economy.verified: Seven coins picked up, then the page hidden and unloaded without the run ending: wallet is 507 after a reload (500 + 7).

persistence.why: A 1.5s throttle left a window iOS could reclaim; a small JSON blob to localStorage costs well under a millisecond, so there was nothing to gain from batching and coins to lose.
persistence.backup: Primary and backup keys. The previous copy rotates to backup before each write - only if it parses, so garbage never overwrites the intact copy. A corrupt primary loads from backup and is repaired immediately, not on the next coin.

lifePause.when: Every life lost except the last
lifePause.rationale: Losing a life is the one moment a runner can pause without breaking flow - momentum is already zero. A mid-run menu would interrupt; a pause at death interrupts nothing. It gives the player a beat to register the loss and a natural point to shop.
lifePause.resume: Tap anywhere, SPACE, or CONTINUE. The resuming input is consumed so it cannot double as a jump; hit-stop is cleared so the world moves at once.
lifePause.guard: A 0.45s lockout swallows input that was already in flight, and only CONTINUE resumes. The button greys to WAIT while locked - a control that silently ignores you reads as broken.

pause.button: Top-right corner of the HUD, live only during a run
pause.screen: Score so far, distance, level, lives and wallet, with RESUME / SHOP / LEADERBOARD / END RUN
pause.rationale: Implemented as a uiScreen rather than a new flag, because update() already freezes the world for any screen other than play - the pause reuses the stop condition the shop and leaderboard rely on.
pause.endRun: Banks the run properly, so a player who wants to stop is not made to die on purpose to post a score.
